saw.short: Tesla's flying Roadster becomes an AI meme machine
saw.headline: Tesla's flying Roadster becomes an *AI meme machine*
saw.what: Tesla unveiled its new Roadster on 15 Oct, shown flipping and flying on cold-gas thrusters. Within a day X filled with AI-made “what if” clips: stuck in traffic, leaping broken bridges, escaping the police, a Back to the Future riff.
saw.why: AI video tools now turn a launch into a meme format in hours, and creators name the tool they used in the post.

saw.short: Hundreds turn out for Lime bike jousting in Hackney
saw.headline: Hundreds turn out for *Lime bike jousting* in Hackney
saw.what: On Saturday two men dressed as knights tried to knock each other off Lime e-bikes in London Fields. It began as a joke post by artist Jack Carden and “Camtholomew the First”. Police let it go ahead, and a sequel is promised.
saw.why: A local in-joke became a real crowd and then went back online as content. Lime got the spotlight without lifting a finger.

saw.short: Strictly fans call out a couple for not saying thank you
saw.headline: Strictly fans call out a couple for *not saying thank you*
saw.what: On Sunday's results show, viewers on social media called Cach Mercer and Maddie Ingoldsby “rude” for not thanking voters after being kept in. Cach later posted an Instagram video thanking his supporters.
saw.why: Audiences now judge the moments between the performance. A thank-you or a tone of voice is part of the content.

saw.short: The UK's Halloween costume of the year: Nikki from Obsession
saw.headline: The UK's costume of the year: *Nikki from Obsession*
saw.what: A BBC round-up on Saturday found fancy dress shops, influencers and make-up artists naming Nikki as the most copied look. One Bournemouth shop says Scream masks make up 20% of its sales; KPop Demon Hunters leads for kids.
saw.why: Costume season is peaking, and the Ramalama (Bang Bang) strut is back as the go-to reveal format.

saw.short: The “Boo” prank is TikTok's trend of the month
saw.headline: The *“Boo” prank* is TikTok's trend of the month
saw.what: People pull a cross-eyed face and say “boo” to camera, often tricking a partner or sibling into joining in. The first known clip (20 Sept) passed 8.4M views; one posted on 12 Oct hit 1.3M in about a day.
saw.why: Low effort, made for a reaction shot and easy to join: a ready-made format for talent if it fits the brand.
saw.source: Know Your Meme, 14 Oct (view counts as reported)

platform.short: Instagram's “Use as reference” makes response Reels easier
platform.headline: Instagram's *“Use as reference”* makes response Reels easier
platform.what: Creators can overlay another Reel (under 90 seconds) in the camera to match a response clip. It's iOS only for now. Instagram is also removing Reels series links on 28 Oct, and Edits adds tappable audio links.
platform.why: Side-by-side recreations are about to get easier on Instagram, so expect more of them in feeds.

platform.short: TikTok Shop UK adds shoppable photo carousels
platform.headline: TikTok Shop UK adds *shoppable photo carousels*
platform.what: UK sellers can turn two or more product images into a swipeable post that links to products, with no video needed. Live shopping also gets group deals and price cuts once a sales target is hit.
platform.why: Brands without video can now sell straight from the feed with product photos they already have.
platform.source: TikTok Shop UK via Social Media Today, 14 Oct

platform.short: LinkedIn brings back the business card
platform.headline: LinkedIn brings back the *business card*
platform.what: LinkedIn is rolling out a digital business card you can design, with your headshot, job title and a QR code, and keep in your phone's wallet. It goes global over the coming months.
platform.why: Events are where B2B relationships start. This makes LinkedIn the default handshake again.
